1: # Instructions
2: 
3: Count the scored points on a Go board.
4: 
5: In the game of go (also known as baduk, igo, cờ vây and wéiqí) points are gained by completely encircling empty intersections with your stones.
6: The encircled intersections of a player are known as its territory.
7: 
8: Calculate the territory of each player.
9: You may assume that any stones that have been stranded in enemy territory have already been taken off the board.
10: 
11: Determine the territory which includes a specified coordinate.
12: 
13: Multiple empty intersections may be encircled at once and for encircling only horizontal and vertical neighbors count.
14: In the following diagram the stones which matter are marked "O" and the stones that don't are marked "I" (ignored).
15: Empty spaces represent empty intersections.
16: 
17: ```text
18: +----+
19: |IOOI|
20: |O  O|
21: |O OI|
22: |IOI |
23: +----+
24: ```
25: 
26: To be more precise an empty intersection is part of a player's territory if all of its neighbors are either stones of that player or empty intersections that are part of that player's territory.
27: 
28: For more information see [Wikipedia][go-wikipedia] or [Sensei's Library][go-sensei].
29: 
30: [go-wikipedia]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go_%28game%29
31: [go-sensei]: https://senseis.xmp.net/

This is the classic Exercism go-counting exercise. The tests import `Board`, `WHITE`, `BLACK`, `NONE` from go_counting.

Implementation:
- `WHITE = "W"`, `BLACK = "B"`, `NONE = ""`
- `Board.__init__(self, board)`: store the board.
- `territory(x, y)`: validate coordinates; if the cell is a stone, return ("", set())... actually, in the case of a stone, the standard exercism solution returns `(NONE, set())` — the test "a_stone_and_not_a_territory" expects stone to be NONE and an empty set.
- Flood-fill the empty region, collect the set of adjacent stones. If the set of stones is exactly {BLACK} → BLACK, {WHITE} → WHITE, otherwise NONE.
- `territories()`: return a dict {BLACK: set, WHITE: set, NONE: set}, iterating over all empty cells and running flood-fill on each unvisited empty cell.

All 11 tests pass. The implementation in `go_counting.py`:

- **Module constants**: `WHITE = "W"`, `BLACK = "B"`, `NONE = ""` (imported by the test file).
- **`Board.territory(x, y)`**: raises `ValueError("Invalid coordinate")` for out-of-bounds coordinates; returns `(NONE, set())` for a stone; otherwise flood-fills the connected empty region (horizontal/vertical neighbors only) and assigns it to `BLACK` or `WHITE` if all bordering stones are that player's, else `NONE`.
- **`Board.territories()`**: flood-fills each unvisited empty cell once and accumulates regions into a `{BLACK: set, WHITE: set, NONE: set}` dict.
